newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-PEDROSO RETAINS LONG JUMP TITLE WITH TWO VALID JUMPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-PEDROSO RETAINS LONG JUMP TITLE WITH TWO VALID JUMPS.

text.p: Ivan Pedroso retained his world men's long jump title on Tuesday after recording just two valid jumps in six attempts.
Pedroso effectively won the competition with his first mark of 8.42 metres, fouling on his next four attempts and finishing with an effort of 7.60.
American Erick Walder was second with 8.38 and Kiril Sosunov of Russia took the bronze medal with his final leap of the competition, recording 8.18.

Cuban Pedroso jumped 8.96 metres at the high altitude Italian ski resort of Sestriere in 1995 but was denied a world record because of allegations that an official had interfered with a wind gauge. He won the world title in Gothenburg in the same year.
He finished 12th at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics after undergoing a hamstring injury in March but has been back to his best this year with the second longest indoor jump ever of 8.60 metres.
